overview: From 2026-08-23 to 2026-08-30, ethereum-optimism/supersim had 1 new PRs (0 merged), 1 new issues, and 16 active contributors.

topIssues.title: Automate the OP Stack upgrade cadence
topIssues.author: jefr90
topIssues.body:
Before ethereum-optimism/supersim#424, supersim's monorepo pin was 14 months stale: `optimism v1.13.4-0.20250617223244-f273e18a17c6` from June 2025, with the last release cut in August 2025.

Catching up was not a version bump. It surfaced package moves (`op-service/predeploys` to `op-core/predeploys`), a go-ethereum rename (`types.TrieHasher` to `types.ListHasher`), and the deletion of `SuperchainTokenBridge` and `SuperchainERC20` from contracts-bedrock, which removed a predeploy and a documented user workflow. None of that is hard individually; it is expensive because 14 months of it arrived at once.

ecosystem#1013 asks whether the cadence should be automated so this does not recur. Filing that as its own issue.

### Suggestion

A scheduled job that runs `just install-monorepo <latest-release>` plus `just check-monorepo-versions`, then builds and tests, and opens a PR when it succeeds or an issue when it fails. Even a monthly failing run is useful, since it dates the breakage instead of letting it accumulate silently.

### Blocked on a prerequisite

This cannot target current releases until ethereum-optimism/optimism is consumable as a Go module again. `op-core/superchain` embeds a gitignored `superchain-configs.zip` that is absent from the published module, so every release after 2026-04-29 fails to build downstream. That is filed separately against the monorepo. Until it is resolved, any automation would pin to `op-node/v1.16.13` and stay there.

topPRs.title: feat: upgrade OP Stack dependency to op-node/v1.16.13
topPRs.author: jefr90
topPRs.body:
Part of #1008 via [ecosystem#1013](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1013).

Moves supersim from a June 2025 monorepo pin to `op-node/v1.16.13` (`6de21d0f`, 2026-04-21), ten months newer, and regenerates genesis against it. Along the way it fixes two things that were already broken on `main`.

## Version gap

`go.mod` was pinned to `optimism v1.13.4-0.20250617223244-f273e18a17c6` (June 2025); last release `0.1.0-alpha.59` (2025-08-06). Roughly 14 months of drift. Both the Go module and the contracts submodule now sit on `op-node/v1.16.13`, so `just check-monorepo-versions` passes.

## Why not the latest release

`op-node/v1.19.5` cannot be consumed as a Go module today:

```
op-core/superchain/chain.go:21:12: pattern superchain-configs.zip: no matching files found
```

Monorepo PR [#20314](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20314) (2026-04-29) added `op-core/superchain`, which `//go:embed`s `superchain-configs.zip`. That zip is **gitignored** and generated locally from the superchain-registry submodule. Verified, not inferred:

- Gitignored at **every** release tag checked (`op-node/v1.17.0`, `v1.18.0`, `v1.19.0`, `v1.19.5`, `op-contracts/v7.0.0`, `v8.0.0-rc.3`); only the `.sha256` is committed.
- The published module confirms it: `…optimism@v1.19.5/op-core/superchain/` has `superchain-configs.zip.sha256` but **no** zip.
- `sync-superchain.sh`'s three documented modes all require a superchain-registry checkout, so none is usable by a module consumer.

supersim reaches it via `genesis/worldgen` → `op-chain-ops/interopgen` → `op-core/superchain`. The monorepo hides this from itself with `just build-superchain-go`, and its container builds carry a melange pipeline whose comment documents this exact error. Neither helps a downstream `go build`.

**Every OP Stack release from 2026-04-29 onward is currently unconsumable as a plain Go dependency.** `op-node/v1.16.13` (2026-04-21) is the newest stable release before it. Fixing that is a monorepo change and needs its own issue.

## Upstream changes absorbed

| Change | Effect |
|---|---|
| `op-service/predeploys` → `op-core/predeploys` | import rewrite across 9 files |
| `types.TrieHasher` → `types.ListHasher` (op-geth) | one-line fix in `interop/indexer_test.go` |
| `SuperchainTokenBridge` + `SuperchainERC20` deleted ([#19999](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19999)) | see below |

### SuperchainTokenBridge removal is the user-facing change worth reviewing

`v1.16.13` is tagged on the commit that deleted these contracts. `SuperchainTokenBridge` (`0x4200…0028`) is gone from the predeploy set; `NativeAssetLiquidity` (`0x…0029`) was added. So this PR drops the predeploy from `interopPredeploys`, deletes `bindings/superchaintokenbridge.go` and its event logging, removes it from the `build-contracts` / bindings recipes and the genesis deploy script, and replaces the README and docs "send a SuperchainERC20 from 901 to 902" walkthrough with a note pointing at `SuperchainETHBridge` and `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger`.

`L2NativeSuperchainERC20` (the `0x420beeF…0001` test token) survives by extending **interop-lib's** `SuperchainERC20`, already a submodule here. Its test moves to interop-lib's `IERC7802`, `ISuperchainERC20` and `PredeployAddresses`, and `@solady-v0.0.245` resolves from interop-lib's vendored copy so the token and its test share one `ERC20` type.

Note this makes supersim's dependence on interop-lib go **up**, which matters for [#1009](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1009)'s sync-vs-deprecate decision.

## Genesis regenerated

`genesis/generated/` is rebuilt against `v1.16.13`. The diff is exactly what the upstream change predicts: the SuperchainTokenBridge implementation at `c0d3c0d3…0028` disappears and a new predeploy implementation at `…002b` appears. The Uniswap V4 addresses move as a consequence, so `interop/applier.go` is updated to match.

This required fixing a **pre-existing bug that made `just generate-genesis` fail on `main`**:

`PositionManagerLib.MODIFIED_BYTECODE` was declared as a plain string literal rather than `hex"..."`, so Solidity stored the ASCII of its 40,940 hex characters (40,940 bytes) instead of the 20,470 decoded bytes. CREATE2 then executed `"6101808…"` as opcodes, which surfaced as `gas uint64 overflow` and aborted with `Create2: Failed on deploy`. A probe confirms the fix: length 40,940 → 20,470, first byte `54` (`'6'`) → `0x61` (PUSH2).

That this predates the upgrade was established with a control run: on unmodified `main`, with the old pin, the published (HTTP 200) artifacts tarball, and the mise-pinned `forge nightly-e5ec47b8`, generation fails identically.

`TestL2ToL2Transfer` is removed: it drove `sendERC20` on the deleted bridge and can never pass against the regenerated genesis. The two remaining `wait.For` loops are now bounded, so an unmet condition fails in seconds rather than stalling until the 10m package timeout.

## CI fixes (both pre-existing)

**`go-tests` had been red on this repo's CI before this branch.** The same failure appears on PR #423. `runCmd` uses `CombinedOutput`, and mise printed `WARN deprecated [alias]: use [tool_alias] instead` to stderr on every `cast` invocation, so the warning was prepended to each command's output and every string comparison failed. The unbounded `wait.For` loops then hit the 10m timeout. Renaming `[alias]` → `[tool_alias]` removes it at source.

**`go-lint`** broke on this branch: golangci-lint v1.63.4 is built with go1.23 and refuses a go1.24.6 target. Only v2.x is still published, and it drops `-e` and moves `goimports` to formatters, so the config moves into `.golangci.yml`. v1's default exclusion presets are opted back in explicitly, otherwise errcheck re-reports every deferred `Close()` v1 never flagged. v2 folds stylecheck and quickfix into staticcheck, surfacing 12 pre-existing issues, which are fixed rather than suppressed.

## Verification

- `just check-monorepo-versions`, `just build-go`, `go vet ./...` clean
- `just lint-go`: 0 issues
- `just test-go`: all 6 packages pass; the root package now completes in ~81s instead of timing out at 600s
- `just build-contracts` / `just test-contracts`: 33/33 Solidity tests pass
- `just generate-genesis` completes end to end for the first time
- A baseline was captured before any change, so none of these are pre-existing failures being papered over

## Remaining, not done here

**No release is cut.** That is the last item on #1013 and may need permissions I do not have.

Three follow-ups are now filed:

1. [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22678](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22678): make `op-core/superchain` consumable by downstream Go modules. This is the one that caps the target version, and it blocks every OP Stack release after 2026-04-29 for any downstream Go consumer, not just supersim.
2. [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22679](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22679): publish contract artifacts for released commits. `just calculate-artifact-url` 404s for this commit, so genesis was regenerated from a local contracts-bedrock build.
3. [#425](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/supersim/issues/425): automate the upgrade cadence, which ecosystem#1013 asks for. Blocked on the first item above.
